transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... well, my family and my friends, they keep bringing it up and saying these bank papers prove nothing was taken from me. But I know better. For over a year now, I’ve known they’re hiding my money. They try to cover it up with all these... these fake bills and fundraisers and trip plans. 

Like my sister’s trip down to the beach. I hate the beach, honestly. The sand gets in your shoes, and the last time I went, I lost my favorite sunglasses. They were these pink ones with little rhinestones on the side? I bought them at a gas station, but they looked real expensive. The guy working the register had this huge tattoo on his neck of an eagle. It looked more like a pigeon, though, his beak was all crooked. 

But anyway, yeah, they use all those trip plans and fundraisers to hide what they're doing with my money, so I just have to keep confronting them. I'm gonna keep at it until they finally tell the truth. I just won't stop asking them. But man, I really miss those sunglasses, they really kept the glare out when I was walking down by the highway...
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you don't seem to hear or see?

Voices? No, I don't... I don't hear people whispering in my head or see ghosts or nothing like that. Just regular stuff. I mean, I hear the neighbor's dog all the time. It's this little brown dog, always digging under the fence by the trash cans. I tried to put some rocks there to stop him the other day, but they were those really heavy landscaping rocks, you know? I actually hurt my back lifting one. It was shaped exactly like a giant potato. 

Which is funny, because I was gonna bake a potato for dinner last night, but my oven is acting all weird. It just makes this clicking noise when I turn the knob. Not a voice, just a... *click click click*. My brother said he'd come over and look at it, but I know he just wants an excuse to snoop around my kitchen drawers and look for my bank statements. He thinks I'm stupid and won't notice him going through my stuff, but I know he's in on it too. He always liked potatoes, though. We used to eat them with just butter and salt when we were kids. But no, I don't hear any weird voices.

Aside from these beliefs about your money, have you noticed any periods where your mood was very low or very high—like feeling extremely sad, hopeless, or unusually energetic and elated—that lasted for days or weeks?

No, I don't get like that. I mean, I'm not sad or bouncing off the walls or anything. I just get mad when they lie to me about my accounts. But I did feel pretty down last week when it rained for three days straight. I hate the rain. It makes my knees ache, right where I fell off my bike when I was twelve. It was a red Schwinn, had a little basket on the front with plastic daisies on it. I loved that bike. I used to ride it all the way down to the corner store to buy those little wax bottles with the juice inside. You know the ones? You bite the top off and drink the juice, and then you can chew the wax like gum. It tastes terrible, like a candle, but I bought them anyway. The guy at the store always gave me an extra one for free. He was nice. He had this big bushy mustache, kind of looked like a walrus. I wonder if that store is still there... I haven't been down that street in years. But anyway, no, my mood's fine, just regular. I just want them to stop stealing from me.
Aside from these concerns about your money, how have you been managing your day-to-day life—like going to work, keeping up with your usual routine, and taking care of yourself?

Oh, I do everything just fine. Other than the yelling matches about them taking my cash, I still handle my own meals and everything. I was actually making a bologna sandwich yesterday and the mustard bottle did that weird sputtering thing, you know when it’s almost empty? It shot yellow stuff right onto my favorite shirt. It’s this black shirt with a wolf howling at the moon on it. I got it at a thrift store for two dollars. The lady tried to charge me three, but I showed her this tiny little hole near the bottom. You really gotta watch people, they'll always try to squeeze an extra dollar out of you. 

But anyway, yeah, I keep my things in order the exact same way I always have. I get myself down to the county clinic and my assistance appointments right on schedule. I usually take the number 4 bus for that. The driver on that route always wears these bright orange gloves, even when it's super hot out. It’s so strange. Like, aren't your hands sweating in there? He honks at pigeons a lot, too. Just lays on the horn if they're walking in the street. Pigeons don't even care about horns, they just waddle away whenever they feel like it. But yeah, my routine is exactly the same and I take care of myself just fine. It's just my family I gotta worry about.
